decisions.statement: A session is a cookie, and nothing keeps a record of a session.
Each site signs its own cookies with a key of its own.
A person is known by the provider that person signs in with and the identifier that provider gives.
An address a provider has not verified signs nobody in.
An address binds a sign-in to a contributor only where that contributor has no sign-in.
A person signing in under an address no contributor names gets a contributor.
A sign-in is a page naming a provider, that provider's identifier, and one contributor.
No cookie crosses from the browser a sign-in opens to the app that opened it.
An app signs in by trading a one-time code for a session of its own.
No app shows a provider's screen in a webview of its own.

definition: who a caller is, and what says so
